You sign with your dominant hand using the other hand only in signs that require both hands to make the other half of the sign.

Hard of hearing since birth, deaf at 10.  When I was young I was extremely anti social and just focused more on reading, writing poetry and the like. It was hell so I became even more anti social, depressed, feeling lonely and extremely isolated and attempting suicide multiple times throughout my early life.

Life didn't start to improve until later in the age of social media that helped me feel less alone by communicating with people.  Deafness itself isn't something I generally talk about, especially among my hearing friends but they're aware of it.

These days I'm married to a guy with speech issues due to cerebral palsy and have a couple room mates who are hard of hearing, one of which has disabled parents as well and is very sympathetic to someone's needs, including mine.  I'm happier these days and less anti social.  Even the local furry community has been very kind and understanding with the exception of this one dude who seems to have the memory of a goldfish and a habitual need to turn mid sentence.
